## How they got there
Real Madrid secured the title by beating Borussia Dortmund 2-0 in the final. Their path was defined by a profile built on elite efficiency, as they recorded 3.0 points per game to be better than 98% of that season's group-phase teams and 15.3 shots per game to rank higher than 97% of their peers. This attacking volume was complemented by exceptional control, with a pass accuracy of 93.1% that surpassed 97% of the league phase competitors.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model would have selected Real Madrid, ranking them second and placing them inside its top two predictions for the season. With a calculated probability of 32.0% to reach the final against a base rate of just 12.5%, the algorithm identified them as a significant outlier among the 16 knockout teams. The model's expected performance corresponded to the quarter-finals, which is the stage nearest to its expectation of 1.36 on the knockout scale.

## Weak spots
The team displayed clear statistical vulnerabilities in their distribution and movement metrics. They executed long passes at a rate of only 7.9% of total passes, a figure better than just 3% of that season's group-phase teams and 2% of all Champions League teams since 2011-12. Additionally, they covered an average distance of 113.1 km per game, which was higher than only 9% of their league-phase rivals and 47% of the historical field.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Better than this %' figures say how many teams the club beat on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where beating a team means having the lower value. Write them as 'better than X% of teams', never as 'top X%'. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.
